title: Website Behavior & Booking Funnel Analysis
text:
Project Overview

This report is part of a larger consulting engagement examining how digital marketing activity translates into customer bookings for a small service-based business. This objective focuses on website behavior and booking funnel optimization. Despite traffic arriving through multiple acquisition channels, the business lacked visibility into where visitors were dropping off and which channels were actually converting. This analysis uses GA4 event-level data to diagnose that gap.


  
    ⚠️
    The Problem
    
      No visibility into where users were leaving the site
      Traffic volume treated as a proxy for success
      Booking form drop-off untracked and unaddressed
      Channel quality vs. volume not distinguished
    
  
  
    ✅
    The Analytical Goal
    
      Map the four-stage booking funnel using GA4 events
      Identify the largest friction point in the user journey
      Segment funnel performance by traffic channel
      Validate patterns through subgroup analysis

title: Website Behavior & Booking Funnel Analysis
text:
Methodology
The method selected is a Descriptive Funnel Analysis using GA4 event-level exports. The funnel maps user progression through four sequential behavioral stages, using total users (not event count) throughout to avoid inflation from repeat-event firing within a single session.

Funnel Stages

  
    
      Sessions
      Entry point — all website visits; denominator for overall conversion rate
    
  
  →
  
    
      Page Views
      Users engaging with site content; surface-level behavioral signal
    
  
  →
  
    
      Form Start
      User begins filling the booking form — highest-intent observable action
    
  
  →
  
    
      Booking Complete
      Form submitted — confirmed booking intent; the conversion event
    
  



Derived Metrics



Metric
Formula




Page View Rate
page_view users ÷ sessions


Form Start Rate
form_start users ÷ page_view users


Booking Rate
booking_complete ÷ form_start users


Overall Conv. Rate
booking_complete ÷ sessions



Traffic channel (GA4 Default Channel Group) is used as the primary segmentation variable, enabling comparison across six acquisition sources: Direct, Organic Search, Organic Social, Referral, Unassigned, and Paid Search.

title: Website Behavior & Booking Funnel Analysis
text:
Key Findings
The funnel narrows sharply and unevenly. The dominant friction point is the transition from page viewing to form initiation — a 91.9% drop-off rate that holds across every traffic channel.

Funnel: Most Users Exit Before Starting the Booking Form


Show figure code
funnel_long <- tibble(
  stage = factor(
    c("Sessions", "Page Views", "Form Start", "Booking\nComplete"),
    levels = c("Sessions", "Page Views", "Form Start", "Booking\nComplete")
  ),
  count     = c(totals$sessions, totals$page_views,
                totals$form_starts, totals$bookings),
  highlight = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

ggplot(funnel_long, aes(x = stage, y = count, fill = highlight)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.52) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(count)),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold", color = "#1A1A1A") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#66ada9", "TRUE" = "#C0392B")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(title = "Most Users Exit Before Completing Any High-Intent Action",
       x = NULL, y = "Users") +
  theme_ao5








Figure 1: Unique users at each stage of the booking funnel. Red bar indicates the largest drop-off point.








Conversion Rate by Traffic Channel


Show figure code
ga4_data |>
  mutate(
    channel   = fct_reorder(channel, overall_conv_rate),
    above_avg = overall_conv_rate > site_avg
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = channel, y = overall_conv_rate, fill = above_avg)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.52) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(overall_conv_rate, accuracy = 0.1)),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.8, fontface = "bold", color = "#1A1A1A") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = site_avg, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#888888", linewidth = 0.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.65, y = site_avg + 0.0025,
           label = paste0("Site avg: ", percent(site_avg, accuracy = 0.1)),
           size = 3.2, color = "#888888", hjust = 0) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("FALSE" = "#7aa496", "TRUE" = "#66ada9")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_ao5 +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "#edf0f7"))








Figure 2: Booking conversion rate by traffic channel. Dashed line = site average.

title: Website Behavior & Booking Funnel Analysis
text:
Recommendations

  
    
      Redesign the Mid-Funnel Experience
      The 91.9% drop-off between page views and form starts is the highest-leverage fix available. Strengthening calls to action, sharpening the value proposition, and reducing booking form friction can increase appointments without requiring additional marketing spend.
    
  
  
    
      Prioritize Organic Search & SEO Investment
      Organic Search converts at 2.3% — more than twice the site average and more than 4× the efficiency of Organic Social. Shifting content and budget investment toward this channel is likely to yield stronger returns than broad social reach alone.
    
  
  
    
      Audit Channel Tracking & UTM Configuration
      Unassigned traffic converts at 3.1% — the highest rate on the site — but its source is currently invisible. Auditing UTM tagging and GA4 configuration to properly classify this traffic is a critical step toward understanding what is driving the best results.
    
  
  
    
      Deploy Purchase Event Tracking via Google Tag Manager
      Current tracking measures booking form submissions — not completed purchases. Configuring GTM to capture purchase completions will allow future analyses to connect marketing activity to actual revenue outcomes, enabling true ROI measurement.

title: Westwood
text:
FILM REVIEW
    WESTWOOD
    Punk. Icon. Activist.
    
    
      DIR. LORNA TUCKER
      ·
      DOCUMENTARY
      ·
      REVIEW BY KATHLEEN JUAREZ
    
  

  
  
    
      “When does someone cease to be a daring provocateur,and become museum worthy?”
    
  




















  
  

    For those unfamiliar with Vivienne Westwood save for her moniker on a clothing label, the designer might strike you as a demure British dame within the first few minutes of director Lorna Tucker's Westwood. Lounging in a tufted chair next to an exquisite floral arrangement, Westwood seems sweet in grandmotherly way, if not eccentric.

    Fast-forward to a few minutes later into the documentary and Westwood leaves you with a very different impression of the designer. The night before her London Fashion Week show, she goes over the minutia of each piece, model, and accessory. Nothing escapes her notice and she berates an assistant for making an egregious error: a judgment call for a small hem on a garment where a large ribbed hem should be. "I don't remember doing this. Fuck them, they're just disgusting. What's with this tiny hem? It's crap," she says.

    
      
      "I don't know what I'm doing, it's a mess. It's my fault, it's just not good."
      — Vivienne Westwood
    

    Director Lorna Tucker's talent comes in the keen juxtaposition of the two sides of Westwood's demeanor. While the documentary is laden with incidences of Westwood's ferocity, it's contrasted with more intimate moments of Westwood at work. Camera panned at a distance, she confides in her husband post tiny-hem tirade, "I don't know what I'm doing, it's a mess. It's my fault, it's just not good." We can see where the weight of her work weighs heavily on her shoulders.

    Several times throughout the documentary, Westwood iterates a version of "If I don't like it, I just won't put it out." Though her desire for complete creative control leads her to be tyrannical at times, Westwood is revealed to be a deeply sensitive, and introspective artist who pours herself into every detail of her work.

    
      ✦
    

    Westwood's work is one of constant rebellion both against the status quo of stuffy English society and at certain points even her own previous designs. One portion of the documentary shows a museum curator from The Victoria and Albert Museum delicately handling Westwood's most famous piece: a muslin t-shirt adorned with a swastika and other subversive imagery. In another moment of brilliant juxtaposition, tinkling classical piano music plays as the curator runs her gloved hand over the inverted cross printed on the shirt.

    The emotional weight of the documentary relies on Westwood examining this question herself. Much of the documentary seems to be Westwood grappling with her name, company, and designs becoming globally known and marketable while still maintaining her artistic integrity as her company is on the verge of becoming a leviathan. "I'm in danger of not being able to control everything properly," she laments.

    
      VERDICT
      Perhaps most poignant about this documentary is the fact that despite having essentially built her career rebelling against the status quo, later Westwood is ironically resistant to change, evident in her fight against climate change and the uncontrollable growth of her own company.
      Overall the film succeeds in taking Vivienne Westwood into the third dimension. The designer is a deeply complicated character and Lorna Tucker takes great care in exploring the intricacies of the designer's psyche over the course of the documentary. Through Tucker's lens, Westwood is more than just a label on a tag; she's a true artist willing to sacrifice monetary gain and fame to maintain her own creative vision.
    

  

  
    
    Written by Kathleen Juarez

title: Tenant Email Notification System
text:
Project Overview

Property Management Office previously relied on a fully manual email workflow: contacts were individually entered into Outlook folders based on tenant self-submitted forms, with no automated way to update, remove, or segment contacts. This project replaced that system end-to-end with a HubSpot CRM, delivering a dynamic, compliant, and analytics-ready email notification platform.

title: Tenant Email Notification System
section: The Challenge: A Broken Manual System
text:
The Challenge: A Broken Manual System
The legacy process for managing tenant communications was outdated and created significant operational overhead and compliance risk.

title: Tenant Email Notification System
text:
The Solution: HubSpot CRM Pipeline

  
    
      Data Migration
      Existing Outlook contacts exported to .xls and bulk-imported into HubSpot, preserving all prior tenant records.
    
  
  
    
      Sign-up Form
      A HubSpot-hosted form published via QR code and short link (Bitly) captures new subscribers automatically.
    
  
  
    
      Dynamic Lists
      Contacts are searchable and filterable. Form submissions auto-create or auto-update records — no manual entry.
    
  
  
    
      Email Campaigns
      One-time blasts or automated sequences with personalization tokens, branded templates, and compliance-ready unsubscribe links.
    
  
  
    
      Analytics
      Delivery, open rate, and click-through rate tracked per campaign — closing the loop on what actually reaches tenants.
    
  


Key Feature Highlights
Dynamic Contact Management: HubSpot’s list engine means contacts are always current. Resubmitting the sign-up form automatically updates an existing record rather than creating a duplicate which solved the stale-data problem that plagued Outlook folders.
Compliant Opt-Out: Every email includes a one-click unsubscribe footer, meeting CAN-SPAM requirements without requiring tenants to contact the office.
Personalization Tokens: Email greetings auto-populate with the tenant’s name, making mass communications feel more personal and increasing engagement.
Delivery Analytics: The HubSpot dashboard tracks delivery status, open rates, and click-through rates per campaign, giving the property management team concrete feedback on communication effectiveness.
Campus-Wide Rollou:t The launch used a printed flyer with QR code, a Bitly short link for digital sharing, and an introductory email to the existing list, inviting tenants to opt in to the new system.

title: Tenant Email Notification System
text:
Outcomes & Impact

  
    ⏱️
    Time Saved
    Eliminated manual contact entry and bounce-back monitoring — routine list maintenance now requires no staff intervention.
  
  
    📈
    Better Reach
    The QR-code and short-link sign-up flow makes it easy to grow the list beyond the original tenant base to campus employees and visitors.
  
  
    🔍
    Visibility
    For the first time, the team can see open rates, click rates, and delivery stats — enabling data-driven improvements to future campaigns.
  
  
    ⚖️
    Compliance
    Built-in unsubscribe links and opt-in forms align the system with email marketing best practices and CAN-SPAM requirements.

What happened
Details




~Apr 2026
Initial GitHub Pages deployment
Set up Quarto project. Configured output-dir: docs in _quarto.yml so rendered files go to /docs.


~Apr 2026
Fixed 404 on live site
GitHub Pages was running Jekyll on Quarto output, ignoring folders starting with underscores. Fixed by creating .nojekyll in /docs.


~Apr 2026
Installed Quarto R package
Resolved 'no package called quarto' error. Switched to quarto render in RStudio Terminal going forward.


~Apr 2026
Fixed duplicate YAML key error
Resolved YAMLException: duplicated mapping key — caused by website: appearing twice in _quarto.yml.


~Apr 2026
Fixed broken CSS/assets on live site
Site appeared unstyled post-publish. Fixed by adding site-url: 'https://kathleenjuarez.com' to _quarto.yml.


~Apr 2026
Connected custom domain
Added 4 A records and a CNAME for www pointing to kathleen-juarez.github.io. DNS propagation took ~4 hours.


~Apr 2026
Renamed styles.css → styles.scss
Quarto threw an unexpected '$' error because the CSS file contained Sass variable syntax. Renamed, moved to theme: list, added /*-- scss:rules --*/ divider.


May 2026
Git branch divergence fix
Resolved non-fast-forward push errors. Workflow: git stash → git restore → git pull --rebase. Root cause: RStudio auto-regenerating a file after stashing.

text:
About This Site



  
    This portfolio was designed and hand-coded by me using  Quarto, HTML, and CSS. No drag-and-drop builders involved!
  

  See how it all came together ↓
  github.com/kathleen-juarez/portfolio-site

  
    
      📘 What's GitHub?
      
        GitHub is a website where people store and share code. Think of it like Google Drive, but specifically designed for software projects. It lets developers save their work, track changes over time, and collaborate with others without overwriting each other's work.
        If you're asking yourself this question, you've clearly never spent the night crying in front of your computer after unsuccessfully trying to push your code to GitHub, merge divergent branches, and then lose your entire document in the process. Ah, to have a layman's innocence.
      
    
  


### What went into it

- **Design** — a custom color palette, typography choices, and layout decisions made entirely from scratch
- **Structure** — Quarto's publishing framework, configured for GitHub Pages with a custom domain
- **Styling** — a multi-file CSS/SCSS architecture: global styles, a hero stylesheet, and page-specific stylesheets for each major section
- **Content** — an editorial-style film review page, a full analytics case study with interactive visualizations, an interactive Flexdashboard, and a styled resume with a custom table of contents

### Tools Used

| Tool           | Purpose                               |
|----------------|---------------------------------------|
| Quarto         | Site framework & rendering            |
| CSS / SCSS     | Custom styling & Bootswatch overrides |
| HTML           | Custom components & page structure    |
| R              | Dashboard templating & rendering      |
| GitHub         | Version control & hosting             |
| Chart.js       | Interactive data visualizations       |
| Flexdashboard  | Analytics dashboard layout            |

    A deliberate six-color palette, a multi-file SCSS architecture, and custom font overrides on top of Bootswatch Minty. Every element — navbar, hero, buttons, headings — styled intentionally rather than inherited by default.

    Dropdown menus, left-justified links, custom font sizing and weight, a tooltip that appears on hover over this very page's nav link — the navbar alone required half a dozen targeted CSS fixes.

    A film review converted into a full editorial layout: drop caps, pull quotes, a full-bleed hero image, floated mid-article photography, and a page-specific tan background — each with its own CSS variables and override logic.
  
  
    📊
    Analytics Case Study
    A full project page featuring interactive Chart.js visualizations from GA4 data, stat cards, data tables, and an embedded 6-slide RevealJS presentation — plus a Flexdashboard with crosstalk-linked filters, scatter plots, and a correlation heatmap.

    Resume Page
    Custom HTML tables, an auto-generated table of contents, SVG decorative dividers, targeted font overrides per section, and university seals sized with pixel-level precision — because markdown tables weren't going to cut it.
  


The site you’re looking at is the sum of 71 logged changes, a handful of 404 errors, at least one Git catastrophe, and a lot of iterating on things that almost-but-didn’t-quite look right. That’s what building something from scratch actually looks like.

title: Site Analytics
text:
Site Analytics
This dashboard tracks real-time visitor activity on my portfolio site using Google Analytics 4 and Looker Studio. Setting it up involved configuring a GA4 property and data stream, embedding a tracking tag directly into my Quarto site, and designing a custom Looker Studio report to visualize the data. The dashboard updates automatically and tracks key metrics including page views, session duration, traffic sources, device types, and visitor locations worldwide





  
  



  Dashboard powered by Google Analytics & Looker Studio · Data refreshes automatically
